chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, both together from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halabi, from Abd al-A'la, client of the family of Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'Indeed, the house in which there is a Muslim person reciting the Quran, the inhabitants of the sky behold it just as the inhabitants of the world behold the radiant star in the sky.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ السَّمَاءِ: Inhabitants of the sky/heavens — the angels and celestial beings who witness human deeds
key_terms.الْبَيْتُ: The house/home — understood as the domestic dwelling where religious practice is centered
key_terms.الْكَوْكَبُ الدُّرِّيُّ: The radiant/brilliant star — a metaphor for spiritual illumination and elevation
key_terms.يَتْلُو الْقُرْآنَ: Reciting the Quran — active, ongoing recitation as a form of worship

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about the spiritual benefit of reciting the Quran at home?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the spiritual luminosity of a home where the Quran is recited. The imagery of a brilliantly shining star visible to the inhabitants of the heavens conveys that Quran recitation elevates a household's status in the unseen realm. This hadith would have resonated powerfully with its early audience, who understood the cosmos as a layered creation in which the angels and celestial beings are aware of human acts of worship.
